purpose: Evidence-linked advanced assessment bank for P6-P7

cases.title: Crossed brainstem signs
cases.prompt: A patient has an ipsilateral cranial-nerve deficit with contralateral limb weakness. What is the most defensible localisation level?
choices: Cerebral cortex
Brainstem
Cerebellar hemisphere
Peripheral nerve
cases.rationale: Crossed cranial-nerve and long-tract findings are a classic localisation pattern for the brainstem. The exact level still depends on the involved cranial nerve and accompanying tract signs.

cases.title: Neglect pattern
cases.prompt: After a right-hemisphere stroke, a patient repeatedly omits items on the left side of space despite adequate primary vision. Which syndrome best fits?
choices: Aphasia
Hemispatial neglect
Apraxia of speech
Anterograde amnesia
cases.rationale: Persistent failure to attend to contralesional space with preserved primary sensory capacity is characteristic of hemispatial neglect, commonly after right-hemisphere network injury.

cases.title: Basal ganglia reasoning
cases.prompt: A patient develops bradykinesia and rigidity without primary weakness. Which system is most directly implicated?
choices: Basal ganglia motor circuits
Primary visual cortex
Dorsal-column system
Auditory pathway
cases.rationale: Bradykinesia and rigidity point toward basal-ganglia motor-circuit dysfunction rather than loss of corticospinal strength.

cases.title: Interpreting executive scores
cases.prompt: A teenager scores poorly on one executive-function test after sleeping four hours and reports severe anxiety. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The score proves frontal-lobe damage
The score confirms ADHD
Interpret within a broader pattern and consider state confounds
Ignore the score entirely
cases.rationale: Single scores are not anatomically or diagnostically specific. Sleep, anxiety, effort, medication and other state factors can materially affect performance and should be integrated with the broader profile.

cases.title: Performance validity
cases.prompt: A validity indicator is below its recommended threshold. What should happen next?
choices: Diagnose malingering immediately
Treat the whole cognitive profile as invalid without context
Integrate multiple validity indicators and contextual information
Convert the score into an IQ estimate
cases.rationale: Performance-validity findings require converging evidence and contextual interpretation; a single indicator is not synonymous with intentional deception.

cases.title: Memory mechanism
cases.prompt: A person recalls remote autobiographical information but struggles to form new episodic memories. Which distinction is most useful?
choices: Encoding/new learning versus remote retrieval
Motor versus sensory cortex
Left versus right cerebellum
Sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone
cases.rationale: The pattern raises questions about encoding/consolidation of new episodic information relative to retrieval of older information; localisation still requires the wider clinical pattern.

cases.title: Focal slowing
cases.prompt: An EEG shows persistent focal slowing over one region. What is the most defensible conclusion?
choices: It proves a tumour
It indicates focal cerebral dysfunction but is not etiologically specific
It diagnoses epilepsy
It confirms ADHD
cases.rationale: Focal slowing can support focal cerebral dysfunction, but it does not by itself identify a specific cause and is not equivalent to an epileptiform discharge.

cases.title: Epileptiform versus slowing
cases.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes an interictal epileptiform discharge from focal slowing?
choices: They are interchangeable labels
Epileptiform morphology can support increased seizure propensity; slowing is a nonspecific dysfunction marker
Slowing is more specific for epilepsy
Neither has clinical relevance
cases.rationale: Epileptiform discharges and slowing answer different questions. Morphology and clinical context matter; neither should be interpreted in isolation.

cases.title: qEEG and ADHD
cases.prompt: A child has an elevated theta/beta ratio on qEEG. What is the most evidence-consistent clinical use?
choices: Confirm ADHD
Rule out ADHD
Use it as one research/adjunctive measure, not a replacement for standard diagnostic assessment
Choose stimulant dose from the ratio
cases.rationale: The American Academy of Neurology practice advisory does not support using the EEG theta/beta ratio as a stand-alone ADHD diagnostic test.

cases.title: ADHD neurofeedback claim
cases.prompt: Which statement best matches the current group-level ADHD neurofeedback evidence?
choices: It is established as superior to standard care
Blinded outcomes show no meaningful overall benefit, although some standard-protocol analyses show small effects
It cures ADHD when cortical learning occurs
Evidence is too sparse to analyse at all
cases.rationale: A 2025 meta-analysis of 38 RCTs found no meaningful group-level benefit on probably blinded ADHD symptoms overall, with small effects in some standard-protocol subsets.

cases.title: Autism neurofeedback claim
cases.prompt: A family asks whether neurofeedback is an established treatment for core autism features. What is the best response?
choices: Yes, established first-line treatment
No study has ever reported benefit
Evidence is heterogeneous and promising in places, but it is not established standard care for core autism features
It is diagnostic rather than therapeutic
cases.rationale: Recent ASD-specific review literature reports positive findings in some studies but substantial heterogeneity and does not justify presenting neurofeedback as established standard care.

cases.title: EMDR efficacy versus mechanism
cases.prompt: Which statement best separates EMDR efficacy from mechanism?
choices: If EMDR works, bilateral stimulation is proven to be the unique mechanism
EMDR can be evidence-based for PTSD while its precise mechanism remains unsettled
Mechanism evidence is stronger than outcome evidence
EMDR has no guideline support
cases.rationale: Treatment efficacy and mechanism are distinct questions. NICE continues to recommend EMDR for specified PTSD presentations, while no single neural mechanism is established as uniquely causal.

cases.title: Polyvagal framing
cases.prompt: How should Polyvagal Theory be presented in a clinical neuroscience atlas?
choices: As settled neuroanatomical fact
As useless because it is debated
As an influential clinical heuristic whose key evolutionary/neuroanatomical premises are contested
As a diagnostic test for autonomic states
cases.rationale: The theory is clinically influential, but important anatomical and evolutionary claims are actively disputed. Clinical usefulness should not be conflated with established biological fact.

cases.title: Intergenerational trauma
cases.prompt: Which statement is most defensible about intergenerational trauma?
choices: Specific traumatic memories are epigenetically inherited
Intergenerational associations can reflect social, developmental and possibly biological pathways; human epigenetic transmission remains uncertain
There is no evidence of intergenerational association
Epigenetics eliminates environmental confounding
cases.rationale: Human intergenerational findings are compatible with multiple pathways. Epigenetic observations do not establish deterministic transmission of specific trauma memories.

cases.title: Autism neuroscience inference
cases.prompt: A group-level imaging study reports an average network difference in autistic participants. What can you conclude about an individual child?
choices: The child must have that neural pattern
The finding confirms autism in that child
Group-level findings do not provide a deterministic individual biomarker without validated individual-level performance
The finding determines treatment choice
cases.rationale: Group differences describe distributions, not deterministic individual signatures. Diagnostic inference requires validated individual-level accuracy and clinical assessment.

cases.title: ADHD biomarker reasoning
cases.prompt: Which approach is most consistent with evidence-based ADHD assessment?
choices: Diagnose from one EEG biomarker
Integrate developmental history, impairment, symptoms across contexts and differential considerations; biomarkers are not stand-alone diagnostic substitutes
Diagnose from processing-speed weakness
Diagnose from response to stimulant medication
cases.rationale: ADHD remains a clinical diagnosis based on symptoms, developmental course and impairment; currently available EEG biomarkers should not replace standard assessment.

cases.title: Clinical localisation before diagnosis
cases.prompt: A patient presents with sudden left facial weakness, left arm weakness and language disturbance. What should come first in neurological reasoning?
choices: Assign a psychiatric diagnosis
Localise the affected system/network and establish time course before deciding aetiology
Order qEEG to diagnose the lesion
Infer personality change from hemisphere side
cases.rationale: Neurological reasoning separates localisation (where) from aetiology (what), while time course sharply constrains the differential.

cases.title: Evidence hierarchy in treatment claims
cases.prompt: A small uncontrolled study reports improvement after a novel brain-based intervention, while multiple blinded RCTs and a meta-analysis show little group-level benefit. How should the Atlas teach the intervention?
choices: Lead with the uncontrolled positive study
Present efficacy as established
Prioritise the higher-level evidence, describe uncertainty, and preserve the positive study as lower-tier/contextual evidence
Remove all references to the intervention
cases.rationale: Evidence synthesis should weight design quality, bias control, replication and directness rather than selectively privileging positive findings.
